title: Component-weighted bias in rotation curve model selection: A proxy-chain audit of χ2-based ∆AIC statistics
description: Audits the standard rotation-curve model selection pipeline (Φ → V(r) → χ2 → ∆AIC) and shows that χ2 weighting induces a structural, component-weighted bias in bulge-dominated galaxies. Introduces a bulge-bias metric B_bulge, quantifies its impact across the SPARC 175 sample, and proposes an RCMB-compliant protocol that reports ∆AICinner and ∆AICouter separately to avoid conflating baryonic-fitting flexibility with halo/modified-gravity performance.

proxy_chain.description: Evaluation pipeline mapping a gravitational potential hypothesis to a single-number model selection statistic.

total_velocity.description: Observed circular speed is the quadrature sum of baryonic components and the halo/modification under test.

chi_squared.description: Standard weighted least-squares misfit with per-point weights w_i = \sigma_i^{-2}.

inner_weight_fraction_B.latex: B = \frac{\sum_{i: r_i < r_c} w_i}{\sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i}, \quad w_i = \sigma_i^{-2}
inner_weight_fraction_B.description: Fraction of total \chi^2 weight contributed by inner radii r < r_c (default r_c = 3 kpc).

component_weighted_bias_Bbulge.description: Weighted average of bulge dominance per data point; estimates how much of \chi^2 is 'spent' on bulge-dominated radii.

bias_condition.description: Operational criterion that flags model-selection bias when inner bulge dominance flips the outer-region model preference.

key_results.main_finding: Bulge-driven component-weighting in χ2 compresses ∆AIC toward baryonic inner regions, biasing model selection; B_bulge correlates with ∆AIC over SPARC (ρ=0.176, p=0.020), rising to ρ=0.474 (p=0.013) in the LATENT regime, and EFC’s win/tie rate drops from 91.9% (B_bulge<0.1) to 44.4% (B_bulge>0.2).
datasets_used: SPARC 175 decomposed rotation curves (Lelli et al. 2016)

sealed_predictions.statement: Adopting the RCMB-compliant protocol (reporting ∆AICinner and ∆AICouter separately) will reduce apparent NFW preference in galaxies flagged by B_bulge > 0.4, with outer-region comparisons shifting toward EFC or neutral (|∆AICouter| < 2) relative to global ∆AIC.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Recompute split ∆AIC on SPARC and future RC datasets; if bulge-flagged systems continue to prefer NFW strongly (∆AICouter ≥ +10) in the outer region, the prediction is falsified.

kill_criteria: KC1: Low-bulge test. In galaxies with B_bulge < 0.1, an RCMB-compliant outer-region comparison (r > 3 kpc) shows strong, consistent preference for NFW over EFC: ≥70% of the sample with ∆AIC_outer ≥ +10 and median ∆AIC_outer ≥ +10. This would indicate an EFC dynamics mismatch outside the baryon-dominated regime.

KC2: Reweighting robustness. Using uniform weights (w_i = 1) or radially balanced weights that suppress inner dominance, EFC remains globally disfavored across low-bulge systems (≥70% with ∆AIC_global ≥ +10). Persistence under de-biased weighting would falsify the bias-based rescue of EFC.

KC3: FLOW-regime failure. In the EFC FLOW regime and with B_bulge < 0.1, EFC’s outer-region residual RMS exceeds NFW by ≥10 km s^-1 in median (or in ≥50% of galaxies), indicating systematically worse halo-scale fits where EFC is expected to perform best.

KC4: Cross-sample replication. On independent high-quality RC datasets beyond SPARC (similar depth and decomposition), the low-bulge outer-region analysis again yields ≥70% of galaxies with ∆AIC_outer ≥ +10 favoring NFW over EFC. Repeatable failure across samples would kill the EFC explanation.
